lessons.title: What is a perp?
lessons.summary: A perpetual contract follows an asset price without requiring you to buy the token or stock.
takeaways: You do not receive BTC, ETH, or a stock: you open a position that moves with that market.
Perps do not expire like traditional futures; they stay open while you have enough margin.
You can close the position whenever you want if the market is available.

example.label: Example
example.value: BTC perp is not BTC spot
example.note: Buying BTC spot means owning BTC. Opening a BTC perp means getting exposure to BTC price.

lessons.title: Margin: the money you put up
lessons.summary: Margin is the collateral you reserve to support a leveraged position.
takeaways: If you put up 100 USDC as margin, that is the base absorbing profits and losses.
Margin is not a fee: it remains yours while the position is healthy.
If the loss gets too close to your margin, liquidation risk appears.

example.label: Example
example.note: With 100 USDC you can open a 100 USDC position at 1x or a larger position if you use leverage.

lessons.title: Leverage: multiplying exposure
lessons.summary: Leverage increases your position size using the same margin.
takeaways: 5x with 100 USDC creates roughly 500 USDC of exposure.
If the market moves 2%, your 5x position moves like roughly 10% on your margin.
Leverage does not increase your chance of being right; it only amplifies the result.

example.label: Quick formula
example.note: A favorable move adds up faster. An unfavorable move also subtracts faster.

lessons.title: Long and short
lessons.summary: Long means betting it goes up. Short means betting it goes down.
takeaways: You open long when you want to profit if price rises.
You open short when you want to profit if price falls.
In both cases you can lose if the market moves against you.

example.label: Direction
example.note: The same candle can be good or bad depending on your position direction.

lessons.title: Liquidation
lessons.summary: Liquidation happens when your margin is no longer enough to cover a large loss.
takeaways: The higher the leverage, the closer the liquidation price gets.
A stop loss can close before liquidation, but it does not guarantee a perfect price.
Never use your entire balance as margin for one idea.

example.label: Mental rule
example.note: This is an approximation. The real price depends on market conditions, maintenance, fees, and funding.

lessons.title: Basic orders
lessons.summary: Market enters fast. Limit waits for a price. Stop helps cut losses.
takeaways: Market prioritizes execution and can have slippage.
Limit prioritizes price, but may not fill.
Stop loss and take profit help define your exit before emotions take over.

example.label: Order
example.note: When starting out, understand which order you are sending before tapping the final button.

lessons.title: Your plan before the trade
lessons.summary: A trade without a plan usually turns into hope. Define entry, exit, and max loss.
takeaways: Decide how much you can lose before opening the position.
Use small sizes while learning how a real position feels.
If you cannot explain the trade in one sentence, it is probably not ready.

example.label: Minimum plan
example.note: Entry: where you open. Invalidation: where you accept you were wrong. Exit: where you take profit or cut the loss.

checklist.title: Checklist before trading
items: I know whether I am long or short.
I know how much margin I am risking.
I understand what my leverage does.
I have an exit point if it goes wrong.
I am not using money I need to live.
